title_en: Single-Manager Hedge Funds, Pod Shops, and the Age of AI – Paul Enright (EP.527)
title_zh: 单一经理对冲基金、Pod Shop 与 AI 时代 —— Paul Enright（EP.527）
subtitle_zh: Paul Enright 用工厂与喜剧类比拆解单一经理与多经理对冲基金的生产逻辑，并分享 AI 时代股票研究中「长半衰期」知识与组合优化的思考。
summary_zh: 本集主持 Ted Seides 对话 Paul Enright——他曾在 Viking Global 长期任职，后创办并管理家族办公室 Creoson Capital，过去三年又重返业界出任多经理平台 Jane Street 基本面股票业务主席。Paul 用「工厂」和「喜剧」类比区分两类对冲基金：单一经理人的核心生产单元是单个卓越想法，多经理平台的产品则是组合本身，靠广度与现代投资组合理论（MPT）分散风险；两者在质量控制、研究、想法生成与组合管理上分工各异。他坦言进入 pod shop 后，对广度、波动率与夏普比率驱动收益有了全新认识。两人深入探讨规模优势、alpha 单元的风险与杠杆，以及股票收益归因（盈利增长 vs 估值倍数扩张），指出当前市场结构性地利好单一经理人，因为难以被系统化的「估值倍数」更依赖个人判断与行为心理学。Paul 还分享 AI 时代的研究方法：把长半衰期知识内化为晶体智力，将短半衰期任务交给 AI，警惕认知负债；并就组合优化、集中度、Kelly 公式、公私合璧混合基金以及未来基金的人才结构给出见解。最后他谈到健康、认知负债与拥抱技术周期的平衡。

turns.zh: 请欣赏我与 Paul Enright 的对话。Paul，很高兴见到你，你好吗？很好。我觉得最好的切入点，是谈谈过去几年你在一家多经理 pod shop 内部的所学。有很多我原以为自己懂、也确实是对的东西。

turns.en: And there are some things that I thought I knew that were probably different. The analogy that I've used, if you think about a hedge fund generically as a factory, and you said, single manager factory, what is your chief unit of production? You would say, it's an exceptional idea. As a single manager, my job is to create and produce
turns.zh: 也有一些我原以为懂的东西，其实可能不太一样。我常打这样一个比方：如果把对冲基金笼统地看作一座工厂，你说这是单一经理工厂，那你的核心生产单元是什么？你会说，是一个卓越的想法。作为单一经理人，我的工作就是创造和生产

turns.en: an exceptional idea. The factory as a whole hopefully can create and produce a portfolio of exceptional ideas. That's the chief unit of production. If you're a multi-manager, the idea is a component, but it's not the product. The product is the portfolio itself. The multi-manager factory is producing a portfolio of portfolios.
turns.zh: 一个卓越的想法。整座工厂则希望能创造并生产出一个由卓越想法组成的投资组合，这就是核心生产单元。而在多经理平台，单个想法只是一个组成部分，并不是产品本身。产品是投资组合本身。多经理工厂生产的是「组合的组合」。

turns.en: An individual an idea is to a single manager as a portfolio is to the multi-manager. Your top 10 ideas at a single manager are going to drive the returns of the single manager. Your top 10 portfolios will drive the return of the multi-manager, those are the equivalencies. The interesting thing then, let's talk about quality control
turns.zh: 单个想法之于单一经理人，正如投资组合之于多经理平台。你在单一经理平台的前十大想法，会驱动整个平台的收益；而你的前十大组合，会驱动多经理平台的收益，这两者是对等的。有意思的是，我们来谈谈质量控制，

turns.en: if we're talking about factories. The quality control layer in a single manager comes in the creation of the idea, the cultivating of the idea. It's more similar to luxury good or Apple. Apple spends all this time, legacy, Apple, Steve Jobs, Johnny Ive, we're making the iPhone. We spend so much time, they've tested it and retested it
turns.zh: 既然我们在讲工厂。单一经理平台的质量控制层，体现在想法的创造和培养过程中。它更像奢侈品或者 Apple。Apple 花了大量时间——传承、Apple、Steve Jobs、Jony Ive——我们在打造 iPhone。我们花了那么多时间，反复测试再测试，

turns.en: and you've obsessed over it so that when it is delivered into the market, it's not being recalled. It feels like there's less risk. Sure, you're sending software updates. We have an S and an SE or maybe it replaces it. We don't sell the iPhone too anymore. That's the upgrading of the idea.
turns.zh: 你为它倾注了心血，所以当它交付到市场时，不会被召回，风险感觉更小。当然，你会推送软件更新。我们有 S 和 SE，或者干脆取代它，iPhone 2 就不再卖了。这就是对想法的升级。

turns.en: On the quality control side, on the multi-manager side, because the unit of production is the portfolio, individual ideas will not be as quality controlled ex ante. You have to be that much more aware and monitoring of how it operates once it's out in the market. If a portfolio is out there, you have more layers of risk
turns.zh: 在质量控制这一侧，多经理平台因为生产单元是投资组合，单个想法在事前不会经过那么严格的质量把控。你必须更加警觉，持续监控它在市场中如何运作。如果一个组合已经在外面了，你就会有更多层的风险

turns.en: management to say, hey, we might need to recall that portfolio. If you bring it back, then you test it again. Maybe you put it back out in the market, or maybe you say, we're going to discontinue that line. I'm not going to have that portfolio anymore. Let's replace it with another portfolio. That's how I've come to think about it.
turns.zh: 管理来判断：嘿，我们可能需要把这个组合召回。召回后你再测试一遍，也许重新投放市场，也许你会说，我们要停产这条产品线，我不再持有这个组合了，用另一个组合来替代它。这就是我的思考方式。

turns.en: It's a crude analogy. There's a lot of merit to that framing of the two different types of businesses. At the portfolio level, what does that imply about the ideas that go into the portfolio that becomes the unit of production for the multi-manager shop? Can I torture this analogy a little bit more? Maybe.
turns.zh: 这是个粗糙的类比，但对这两种不同商业模式的框架很有价值。那么在组合层面，这对于构成组合的那些想法——也就是多经理平台的生产单元——意味着什么？我能再把这个类比折腾一下吗？也许可以。

turns.en: Like if we switch from a factory analogy to more of a comedy analogy. And you said, a single manager is like a stand-up comedian. They're going to get up on stage. It's scary. They're there by themselves. Maybe they have a couple of analysts who are joke writers. Your job as a joke writer is to give me one great joke
turns.zh: 如果我们从工厂类比切换到喜剧类比。你说，单一经理人就像一位脱口秀演员，他们要上台，这很吓人，他们孤身一人，也许有几个写段子的分析师。你作为段子写手的工作，就是给我一个绝妙的段子，

turns.en: that I can stand up and I can stand behind. That's the equivalent of a single idea. A multi-manager portfolio manages more like a showrunner. I need to produce a bunch of shows and you write the show. An analyst has to come together with a packaged show. What's not one joke in the show? How does it all fit together?
turns.zh: 让我能站起来、能撑得住。这就相当于单个想法。而多经理组合的管理更像一位剧集总监（showrunner）。我要制作一堆节目，你来写这个剧。分析师必须把一个打包好的剧凑出来，不是一个段子，而是整个剧怎么串在一起？

turns.en: You got to tell more stories. I need a package of ideas that go together that will fit into this portfolio because one single idea isn't that important. Part of the reason why that is is because multi-managers are more premised on managing risk under modern portfolio theory where you want breath, you want diversity.
turns.zh: 你得讲更多故事。我需要一整套彼此契合、能装进这个组合的想法，因为单个想法没那么重要。之所以如此，部分原因在于多经理平台更立足于在现代投资组合理论下管理风险，你要的是广度，要的是多样性。

turns.en: A single idea has much less relevance in the portfolio of a multi-manager than it does in the portfolio of a single manager. Great, you like this idea. I need six around the same theme. It's a package, it's a sleeve. Different people call it different things. You need a lot of those. And you put those all together
turns.zh: 单个想法在多经理平台组合中的相关性，远低于它在单一经理人组合中的相关性。好，你喜欢这个想法，我需要围绕同一主题再有六个。它是一个套餐，一个 sleeve（组合分块），不同人有不同叫法。你需要很多这样的套餐，把它们全都放到一起，

turns.en: and that's how you get a portfolio whereas on the single manager side, each individual idea comes together. The risk happens here because all the ideas might look and be the same, then you have hugely high correlation, a lot of volatility, a lot of risk. You've thought about each one of them independent
turns.zh: 这就是你构建组合的方式；而在单一经理这一侧，每个想法各自独立成形。风险就在这里出现，因为所有想法可能看起来、实际上都一样，于是你有极高的相关性、很大的波动、很大的风险。你以为每个想法都是独立思考出来的，

turns.en: that you don't realize that they're all the same thing. Over here, the risk is that you have five great ideas in there. You treat them like all the other ideas. It gets diluted down by everything else. This is less risky, but maybe you don't capture your best ideas all the time.
turns.zh: 却没意识到它们其实是同一件事。而在多经理这边，风险是你有五个很棒的想法在里面，却把它们和其他所有想法一视同仁，被其他东西稀释掉了。这边风险更小，但也许你并不能总是抓住你最好的想法。

turns.en: If we move away from the analogy and go to the day to day work, it feels like there's two different functional roles. There's the analysts coming up with the idea and either side and there's the portfolio manager putting it together. How do each of those look different at the multi-manager and the single manager shop?
turns.zh: 如果我们跳出类比，回到日常工作，感觉有两种不同的职能角色：一边是想出想法的分析师，另一边是把想法组装起来的组合经理。这两种角色在多经理平台和单一经理平台各自有什么不同？

turns.en: If you had three units of time and you said, someone's got to do the research, someone's got to do the idea generating and someone's got to do the portfolio management. At a single manager, an analyst does almost 100% of the research. Maybe it's 90% and a portfolio manager does 10%
turns.zh: 如果你有三个单位的时间，说：得有人做研究，得有人做想法生成，还得有人做组合管理。在单一经理平台，分析师几乎做 100% 的研究，也许是 90%，组合经理做 10%，

turns.en: or maybe a portfolio manager mirrors some percentage of it so that they feel like they're in the sweet spot. It's almost independent. You do 100% of the digging. It's your job to cover this ownness, come up with something and say, I think I have something. That starts the conversation.
turns.zh: 或者组合经理会复刻其中一部分，好让自己感觉处在最佳位置。研究几乎是独立的：你做 100% 的挖掘工作，你的职责是覆盖这个领域，拿出点东西，然后说，我觉得我发现了点什么。这就开启了对话。

turns.en: The idea generation process depends on how senior the analyst could be 60, 40, it could be 70, 30, but it's a shared process. At some point, your analyst is super independent and could be 100% idea-driven and they're only pushing ideas up but it's still a pretty shared process. The portfolio manager's job is that 100% own the portfolio.
turns.zh: 想法生成的过程取决于分析师有多资深，可能是六四开、七三开，但这是一个共享的过程。到了某个阶段，你的分析师非常独立，可能 100% 由想法驱动，他们只是不断把想法往上推，但这仍然是相当共享的过程。组合经理的职责是 100% 拥有这个组合。

turns.en: Once we decide that's a good idea, I'll take it from there. I'll figure out how to do it, size it, how to get it in, how it fits with everything else. In the multi-manager research, idea generation portfolio management, same three things, but the portfolio management piece becomes a little bit more shared
turns.zh: 一旦我们确定这是个好想法，剩下的我来接手。我会想清楚怎么做、怎么定仓位、怎么建仓、它如何与其他一切相契合。在多经理平台，研究、想法生成、组合管理还是这三件事，但组合管理这一环变得更共享一些，

turns.en: because you're not just asking for an individual idea. You like that idea, what are you gonna pair with? The analyst job I would argue at a multi-manager is a lot harder because a lot more is put on them. They have to do the research, they have to come up with ideas and then they need to package it together
turns.zh: 因为你要的不只是单个想法。你喜欢那个想法，那你要用什么和它配对？我认为多经理平台分析师的工作要难得多，因为他们身上背负的东西更多。他们要做研究，要想出想法，然后还要把它们打包在一起，

turns.en: to help the portfolio management, some amount of portfolio management is pushed down to the analyst in a multi-manager mid-layer that is not done in the same way as a single manager. So the extent that the single manager PM is focused mostly on the portfolio construction, you'd think that maybe they have time to say,
turns.zh: 去帮助组合管理。在多经理平台，一部分组合管理被下放给了分析师这个中间层，而这在单一经理平台并不是以同样的方式进行的。所以，鉴于单一经理平台的组合经理主要专注于组合构建，你会想，也许他们有时间去说，

turns.en: they're these individual ideas, how can we package them together so it delivers a robust portfolio? The single managers that do it best are focused on exceptional ideas and exceptional portfolio construction. The enemy of exceptional ideas is mediocre portfolio construction or solid initial good portfolio construction,
turns.zh: 这里有这些单个想法，我们如何把它们打包在一起，交付一个稳健的组合？做得最好的单一经理人，既专注于卓越的想法，也专注于卓越的组合构建。卓越想法的敌人，是平庸的组合构建，或者说初始的组合构建扎实，

turns.en: but not a sophisticated risk management around the portfolio construction as you phase volatility. As you stepped into this, you said there were some things you learned along the way. What were the most surprising aspects of being inside the multi-manager shop that you didn't appreciate from being outside?
turns.zh: 但在组合构建上缺乏围绕波动率的精细化风险管理。当你踏入这一行时，你说有些东西是你一路走来才学到的。身处多经理平台内部，最让你意外、是你在外面时没能体会到的方面是什么？

turns.en: The execution of modern portfolio management theory and the square of the sum of the squares math, the diversification benefits you get by having more ideas and more portfolio. I understood that conceptually. A lot of people will talk about factor neutral beta neutral of this, breath having a lot of ideas,
turns.zh: 现代投资组合理论的落地执行，那个「和的平方对平方的和」的数学，以及通过拥有更多想法和更多组合所获得的分散化收益。这在概念上我是理解的。很多人会谈因子中性、贝塔中性，谈广度、拥有大量想法，

turns.en: a lot of diverse ideas is incredibly important. It's a batting average business. Single managers more of a slugging percentage, best ideas from most, I had no idea. Totally close, I thought I'd walk in like, oh, this is the magic model. The Wizard of Oz behind the curtain, you get some sense of this is how idiosyncratic risk is different.
turns.zh: 大量多样化的想法极其重要。这是一个打击率（batting average）的生意。单一经理人更像是长打率（slugging percentage），从最多的想法里选出最好的那些，我完全不知道。真没想到，我以为我走进去会觉得，哦，这就是那个神奇的模型，是《绿野仙踪》幕后的巫师，你会对特质风险如何不同有某种感觉。

turns.en: No, it's just a model, trying to back test and predict things. It's the emphasis on breath because volatility and sharp drive returns a multi-manager at a single manager which you care about is long short spread how you apply your gross and net to that potential long short spread. That was surprising to me.
turns.zh: 不，它只是一个模型，试图回测和预测。重点在于对广度的强调，因为波动率和夏普比率驱动着多经理平台的收益；而在单一经理平台，你在意的是多空价差，你如何把总敞口和净敞口应用到那个潜在的多空价差上。这让我很意外。

turns.en: I've never been a high velocity of ideas person. I'm interested in the things I'm interested in if I'm not interested, my eyes will gloss over. When you hear pitch after pitch after pitch and you're like, that's fine, that's fine. And then you're like, oh, that was awesome. That's exciting as a single manager.
turns.zh: 我从来不是一个想法高速迭代的人。我只对我感兴趣的东西感兴趣，如果不感兴趣，我就会眼神呆滞。当你一个接一个地听路演，觉得「这个还行，这个还行」，然后突然「哦，那个太棒了」，这在单一经理人身上是很兴奋的。

turns.en: When breath is your goal, you need all the ideas. It's hard to get excited about all the ideas. You're like, hey, that's fine. I always had the luxury of being like, that's not great, I don't wanna do that. I rather be in cash. And it's like, oh, that's a great one. Let's do that. I'm wired that way. I'll always be wired that way.
turns.zh: 当广度是你的目标时，你需要所有的想法。要对所有想法都感到兴奋很难。你会说，嘿，这个还行。我一直有那种奢侈，可以说「这个不够好，我不想做，我宁愿持有现金」，然后「哦，那个很棒，我们做那个」。我就是这么被设定的，将来也一直是。

turns.en: As the pot shops have scaled, clearly breadth benefits from scale. What are some of the other ways that scale has accrued to the benefit of the multi-manager shops? The thing that we can say definitively about the hedge fund industry when I broke into it was there was more talent than capital.
turns.zh: 随着这些 pod shop 规模扩大，显然广度受益于规模。那么规模还以哪些其他方式给多经理平台带来好处？关于对冲基金行业，我能确定地说的是，我入行时，人才比资本多。

turns.en: If you wanted to be an investor and you were talented, Tiger was the only game in town in the late 90s. The idea that there is all this density of talent there in this industry that had not yet scaled makes sense. Then like any diffusion into the economy, 10 of those great investors go and do 10 different things. They hire 10 people.
turns.zh: 如果你想成为一名投资者，又有才华，在 90 年代末 Tiger 是唯一的选择。这个行业里存在如此密集的人才，而它尚未规模化，这说得通。然后就像任何向经济体扩散的过程一样，那 10 位伟大的投资者各自去做 10 件不同的事，各自雇 10 个人。

turns.en: So now you've got 100. It makes sense that the talent would get to fuse. One of the great things that Viking was we had great talent density there. And we were always competing for capital at various points. And then you get bigger during the early years. Well, we have way more talent than we have capital.
turns.zh: 于是现在你有了 100 人。人才会扩散开来是说得通的。Viking 的一大优点就是我们那里有极高的人才密度，而在不同阶段我们一直在争夺资本。早年你会越做越大——好，我们的人才远多于资本。

turns.en: And then after a while, you feel like you're in equilibrium. As the multi-managers have scaled, the benefit is they have more capital than they have talent. Therefore, they become the magnet for the talent. That is a huge benefit. The second thing is that when you have scale, you can create a center book behind it.
turns.zh: 过一阵子，你会觉得达到了均衡。随着多经理平台规模扩大，好处是它们的资本多于人才，因此它们成了人才的磁铁。这是一个巨大的优势。第二点是，当你有了规模，你就能在其背后建立一个中央账簿（center book）。

turns.en: The opportunity to have breadth of ideas to see all the different pockets of ideas and run a center book on top of that. That's an amplifier. It's almost pure margin on top of that. The other way that there's real scale is in the data layer, having the access to be able to acquire and trial and error
turns.zh: 拥有想法的广度、看到所有不同的想法角落，并在此之上运营一个中央账簿的机会，这是一个放大器，几乎是在此之上的纯粹边际收益。规模真正体现的另一个方面是数据层，拥有获取渠道，能够尽可能多地去获取和试错各种数据，

turns.en: as much data as possible and have teams that can analyze that data so that it's not necessarily put onto the investor or the analyst themselves. So much of the challenge with data during my career, whether as an investor and looking at companies that extract data or transform data or anything along that continuum,
turns.zh: 并拥有能分析这些数据的团队，这样就不必把这项工作全压到投资者或分析师本人身上。在我职业生涯中，数据的挑战很大一部分——无论是作为投资者去审视那些提取数据、转换数据或处于这条连续谱上任何环节的公司——

turns.en: most of the time was spent getting the data into the usable format, putting it in the right place. Very little time is spent analyzing the data. There's real scale to being able to throw a team at that. We're going to get the data, scrub it, figure out what structure, what's unstructure, we're going to put it in a place,
turns.zh: 大部分时间都花在把数据变成可用格式、放到正确的位置上，很少有时间用来分析数据。能派一个团队去做这件事，是有真正的规模效应的。我们会去获取数据、清洗它、弄清哪些是结构化的、哪些是非结构化的，把它放到一个地方，

turns.en: and then we're going to deliver to you in a form that's usable when you layer AI on top of that. You have better access to capital. That's a benefit. All of those are huge benefits of scale. So much of the concept of alpha generation in equities is finding the better idea or a portfolio of ideas that's better than the market.
turns.zh: 然后以可用的形式交付给你。当你在此之上叠加 AI 时，你就有了更好的资本获取渠道，这是一个优势。所有这些都是规模带来的巨大好处。股票中 alpha 生成的概念，很大程度上在于找到更好的想法，或者一个比市场更好的想法组合。

turns.en: It's often hard to get your head around that more breath, more ideas somehow could be better than the market than a smaller group of ideas. When you saw it in practice, how did you wrestle with it? Somehow there's still a unit of alpha that's being monetized, risk-managed, supersized through average. This is probably another area
turns.zh: 人们往往很难理解：更多的广度、更多的想法，怎么就可能比市场、比一小撮想法更好。当你在实践中看到它时，你是怎么挣扎消化它的？不知怎么的，仍然有一个 alpha 单元在被货币化、被风险管理、被规模化放大。这大概是另一个

turns.en: that I have better visibility and better understanding of now than I would have had five years ago. A unit of alpha has a volatility component and a risk component to it. You might have a better, more exceptional idea that has a different volatility profile and different risk profile.
turns.zh: 领域，我现在比五年前有了更清晰的视野和更好的理解。一个 alpha 单元有波动率成分和风险成分。你可能有一个更好、更卓越的想法，它有不同的波动率特征和风险特征。

turns.en: Therefore, you don't want to apply a lot of leverage to it. On the other side, you might have something that has less alpha content to it, but it has a type of alpha content that when it's packaged with other ideas, reduces the amount of risk, the way you get your risk is you add the leverage. On an unlevered basis, apples to apples,
turns.zh: 因此你不想对它施加太多杠杆。另一方面，你可能有一个 alpha 含量较低的想法，但它那种类型的 alpha，在与其他想法打包时，能降低风险总量。你获取风险的方式是加杠杆。在无杠杆、同类可比的基础上，

turns.en: what you would find is that those returns would not nearly be as good as that exceptional return because you've shrunk what you would consider as less measurable risk to a more measurable size and more measurable unit of production. Then we'll lever the hell out of it because we'll take leverage as the form of risk.
turns.zh: 你会发现那些回报远不如那个卓越的回报，因为你把原本较难衡量的风险，收缩成了一个更可衡量的规模、更可衡量的生产单元。然后我们会给它加上大量杠杆，因为我们把杠杆当作风险的形式。

turns.en: You can't have concentration, volatility, and leverage together. You're dead. Those are all strange bad followers. You got to pick one or two of them. If you're levered, concentrated, and volatile, I guarantee you you're going to have... There's been a few problems. There's a problem. There's problems along the way.
turns.zh: 你没法同时拥有集中度、波动率和杠杆，那样你就死定了。它们都是糟糕的伙伴，你只能选其中一两个。如果你既有杠杆、又集中、又高波动，我保证你一定会……已经出过几次问题了。有问题，一路上都是问题。

turns.en: I'd love your perspective on what this means at the industry level. Big picture, take a step back. If you think about 25 years of the attribution of stock returns,
turns.zh: 我很想听听你对这在行业层面意味着什么的看法。往大了看，退一步。如果你想想过去 25 年股票回报的归因，

turns.en: put aside dividend, and dividend reinvestment, you just say there's two components to stock returns. One is earnings growth, one is multiple expansion or contraction. That is wildly inconsistent over time. People might give you averages, but if you looked on a year-by-year basis, I broke into the industry in 98,
turns.zh: 把股息和股息再投资放一边，你就说股票回报有两个组成部分：一个是盈利增长，一个是估值倍数的扩张或收缩。这在时间上极不一致。人们也许会给你一个平均值，但如果按年度看，我 98 年入行，

turns.en: so I've looked back to 98 to through 2025. You went through periods, especially early on, where most of the attribution to stock performance was earnings growth. It makes sense to me that the industry would gravitate towards how do we predict earnings? If you can predict earnings, then you can predict the stock.
turns.zh: 所以我回看了 98 年到 2025 年。你会经历一些时期，尤其在早期，股票表现的大部分归因是盈利增长。这在我看来，行业会向「我们如何预测盈利」靠拢是说得通的。如果你能预测盈利，那你就能预测股票。

turns.en: If you look at 2011 through 2025, we switched. There's a couple of weird years in it. Most of it is two-thirds of returns in any given year on a pretty consistent basis were multiple expansion. What is the system for hedge funds, for multi-managers, single managers, whoever, for stock pickers, for trying to understand
turns.zh: 如果你看 2011 到 2025 年，情况切换了。中间有几个怪异的年份，但大部分时间里，在相当稳定的基础上，任意一年三分之二的回报来自估值倍数扩张。那么，对于对冲基金、多经理、单一经理，无论谁，对于选股者，对于试图理解

turns.en: what leads to multiple expansion and multiple contraction over periods of time? That's an opportunity. The entire industry is focused on earnings. If you get the earnings right, you get the stock right. Maybe not. It's less of a predictor. Structurally, you have the entire world now focused on earnings earnings earnings.
turns.zh: 什么导致估值倍数在一段时间内扩张和收缩，这套体系是什么？这就是机会所在。整个行业都盯着盈利，如果你把盈利判断对了，股票就看对了。也许并非如此，它的预测作用在下降。从结构上看，你现在有整个世界都在盯着盈利、盈利、盈利。

turns.en: We're getting to the end of 2026 and the debate could be, I'm focused on 27 earnings, so I'm going to say, you're a chunk, 27? I at 28, if you just look to 28, close my eyes, I'm going to make all this money. Now it's gotten a little bit more quarter by quarter. There's no debating that.
turns.zh: 我们快到 2026 年底了，争论可能是，我盯着 27 年的盈利，所以我会说，你一大块押在 27 年？我押 28 年，如果你只看 28 年，闭着眼睛，我要赚大钱了。现在它变得更逐季了，这一点没有争议。

turns.en: Even quarter by quarter, Muse and Meta is the perfect example. Everything that's happened to Meta in the last two or three months is this document really volatile has been multiple. Muse is this amazing thing. Wow, multiple goes up. I still got to raise money and Muse isn't monetized. Multiple comes down.
turns.zh: 即便逐季看，Muse 和 Meta 就是完美的例子。过去两三个月 Meta 发生的一切——这只波动极大的股票——都是估值倍数在作祟。Muse 是个了不起的东西，哇，倍数上升。我还是得融资，而 Muse 没有被货币化，倍数就下来了。

turns.en: Bobby and I have talked about this. Bobby's always funny with the way he'll distill things. Bobby would be like, such as vibe, multiples just vibe. And I'm like, it's not vibe. There are reasons and you can study it. Historically, it changes. If we did a study, you would say, how earnings move determines what the multiple will do.
turns.zh: Bobby 和我聊过这个。Bobby 提炼事物的方式总是很有趣。Bobby 会说，这就是一种感觉，倍数纯粹靠感觉。而我会说，这不是感觉，是有原因的，你可以去研究它。历史上它会变化。如果我们做一项研究，你会说，盈利如何变动决定了倍数会怎么走。

turns.en: If you get a revenue beat, it usually leads to a more sustainable multiple expansion. Revenue growth seems more durable. If you get a revenue beat with gross margin expansion, that's a better combination. Good revenue growth with flat to declining margins. There's not quite as good. There are reasons why multiples expand
turns.zh: 如果你有一次营收超预期，它通常会带来更可持续的倍数扩张。营收增长似乎更持久。如果营收超预期同时毛利率扩张，那是更好的组合。营收增长不错但利润率持平或下滑，就没那么好了。倍数扩张是有原因的，

turns.en: more important than that. A huge contributor to performance has been the derading ahead of some big secular fear. A big component of this is interest rates. Multiple's dramatically went up because people started to say, what if the terminal is not five and it's four or three now two?
turns.zh: 比这更重要的是，业绩的一大贡献来自在某个重大的长期性恐慌之前的重定价。其中很大一部分是利率。倍数急剧上升，是因为人们开始说，如果终端利率不是 5%，而是 4%、3%，现在是 2% 呢？

turns.en: And now it's like, well, what if the terminal is not two? But three before but five, how much of it is that? That's a fair question. Industry structure doesn't matter whether it's single manager, multi manager. Everyone's focused on earnings. Everyone's really good at earnings now in a way that they weren't what I started.
turns.zh: 而现在又变成，如果终端利率不是 2%，而是 3%，之前是 5% 呢？这其中有多少是这个因素？这是个合理的问题。行业结构无关紧要，无论单一经理还是多经理，每个人都盯着盈利。如今每个人都非常擅长盈利预测，这在我刚入行时可不是这样。

turns.en: A lot of the differentiating factor is this amorphous multiple. It is a little vibe of this is just going to work. This is the regime wherein structurally that benefits the single manager because the individual idea becomes more important. It's hard to systematize multiple. You can systematize earnings. We know what our models are doing.
turns.zh: 很多差异化因素来自那个难以捉摸的估值倍数。它就是一种「这事成得了」的感觉。这种宏观环境从结构上利好单一经理人，因为单个想法变得更重要了。倍数很难被系统化，盈利你可以系统化。我们知道我们的模型在做什么。

turns.en: We know where our earnings are. We know we are versus consensus. This quarter, neck quarter, as the updates come in and consensus starts moving, we can track it multiples harder. How do you systematize and create a process around multiple versus the individual knowing that's going to work and the multiples going to expand?
turns.zh: 我们知道我们的盈利在哪里，知道我们相对于一致预期如何，这个季度、下个季度，随着更新进来、一致预期开始移动，我们能追踪它。倍数更难。你要怎么围绕倍数建立一套流程，而不是靠个人判断它能不能成、倍数会不会扩张？

turns.en: How have you thought about or seen people trying to play with the behavioral psychology part of markets to get to a point where it's not just a one-off guess? It's part psychology and it's part being comfortable saying this isn't just about stock picking. There's this identity in being like, I don't do macro.
turns.zh: 你是怎么思考、或者看到人们如何尝试利用市场的行为心理学部分，以达到不只是一次性猜测的程度？这部分是心理学，部分是能坦然说出「这不只是选股」。当一名选股者有一种身份认同，就是「我不做宏观」。

turns.en: I'm a stock picker, we care, we ignore it. The stock picker vibe is I'm focused on. There's a good business. It's going to earn $10 and five years. It'll trade at 20 times. The 20 times, who cares? 20, 22, 23, 20, 18, whatever. You just make up a multiple because the earnings are what matters most. Brad Jacobs has this great quote.
turns.zh: 我是选股者，我们在意，我们忽略它。选股者的调调是：我专注的是一家好生意，它五年后会赚 10 美元，会以 20 倍交易。那 20 倍，谁在乎？20、22、23、20、18，随便。你就编一个倍数出来，因为盈利才是最重要的。Brad Jacobs 有句很棒的话。

turns.en: You get all the little things right and get the big thing wrong. It's not going to matter. That's true in earnings too. You get all the little data points right. But if you are picking what you think is great long in a sector that's not going to get the multiple because of where we are in a cycle or in a regime,
turns.zh: 你把所有小事都做对了，却把大事搞错了，那没关系。这在盈利上也是如此。你把所有小数据点都对上了，但如果你选了你认为是极好的多头，却处在一个因为我们在周期或宏观环境中的位置而拿不到倍数的行业里，

turns.en: there's this overhang that might be more important than what you think I have this image in my mind. Every sector is always flashing yellow green or red. If you are a traditional long short neutral fund more on the multi-manager camp, you might always want to think that everything's always yellow.
turns.zh: 就有这么一片阴影，可能比你以为的更重要。我脑子里有这么一幅画面：每个行业随时都在闪烁着黄、绿或红。如果你是一只传统的多空中性基金、更偏多经理阵营，你可能会一直想认为一切都是黄色的。

turns.en: You can always find equal longs, equal short. In practice, everybody knows that's not true. Sectors are always flashing green or red most of the time. If you're picking a stock in a flashing green sector, you're probably going to get multiple expansion way better than you think for some period of time.
turns.zh: 你总能找到等量的多头、等量的空头。实践中，每个人都知道这不是真的。行业大多数时候都在闪绿或闪红。如果你在一个闪绿的行业里选股，在一段时间里，你很可能获得比你以为的好得多的倍数扩张。

turns.en: But you have to be aware that's at least influenced by the backdrop. If the macro backdrop is pro cyclical, you're going to get even more multiple expansion. If interest rates are declining versus rising, you're probably going to get even more multiple expansion. There is some psychology to it. There are other things outside of the stock
turns.zh: 但你必须意识到，那至少受到大背景的影响。如果宏观背景是顺周期的，你会得到更多的倍数扩张。如果利率在下行而非上行，你很可能得到更多的倍数扩张。这里面有一些心理学，也有股票本身之外的其他东西

turns.en: that contribute to multiple, which makes it more of a breath of a skill set versus that earning space of it. When you pull away from these components that are increasingly complex in trying to get a stock right in the spirit of time where there's a lot of money to put it up, there's also a lot of money to index funds.
turns.zh: 在促成倍数，这使它更是一种广度的技能组合，而不是只盯着盈利那一块。当你从这些为了把一只股票判断对而变得日益复杂的组成部分中抽身出来——恕我直言——现在有大量的钱投向主动管理，也有大量的钱投向指数基金。

turns.en: A lot of money in quants and CTA is too. How do you think about the potential for whether it's a single-mander multi-manager to have enough of an edge that they can beat the market over time going forward? I used to think that edge was, I'm going to see something that nobody else has seen. I'm going to therefore make an investment
turns.zh: 也有很多钱涌向量化和 CTA。你怎么看，无论是单一经理还是多经理，未来是否有足够的优势，能够长期跑赢市场？我过去以为那种优势是：我会看到别人没看到的东西，因此我会做一笔投资，
